_batch: Phase 2 mini-batch — steam-specific conditional rows, shipped WITH the boiler merge
_note: THE MERGE DOES NOT LOCK IN THE WASH-OUT. Forced-draft, natural-draft and steam boiler measured 100% identical because the mined content was thin and the Phase 2 D/E fill was written at the type level. These are the steam-specific rows that difference should always have contained. They are CONDITIONAL — a hot-water boiler answers NR, per the ruled variant principle, and no template forks.
subject: BOILER — steam conditional rows
source_master: DRAFTED — the differences the type-level fill washed out.

_anchors.CSA B51: boiler, pressure vessel and pressure piping code
_anchors.TSSA: Ontario AHJ — boiler registration and inspection

_conditional: Every row below applies to STEAM boilers. A hot-water boiler answers NR. The Heating Medium pattern: the shape is data, not a fork.

items.label: STEAM: gauge glass installed, clear, and its try-cocks / blowdown valves operable
items.note: The gauge glass is the operator's only direct sight of water level; a fouled one is a boiler run blind.

items.label: STEAM: water column blown down and proven to re-establish level
items.note: A water column that does not blow down cleanly is reporting the level in its own sediment, not the boiler's.

items.label: STEAM: bottom and surface blowdown valves installed, tagged and accessible; discharge to an approved receptor
STEAM: boiler registered with TSSA; CRN and inspection record attached
items.convergence_reason: ONTARIO CODE REQUIREMENT — TSSA registers and inspects steam boilers as pressure vessels. No national source in the anchor set carries the registration step, so it is kept on a stated jurisdictional basis.

items.label: STEAM: primary low-water cutoff proven by lowering the actual water level, not by lifting the float
items.note: The steam LWCO differs from the hot-water one: it must prove against a level that is moving and a vessel that is making steam. Lifting the float proves the float; dropping the level proves the installation.

items.label: STEAM: secondary / auxiliary low-water cutoff proven independently, with manual reset
items.note: Two independent cutoffs is the steam requirement that hot-water boilers do not carry.

items.label: STEAM: safety valve lifted and proven to reseat; capacity verified against boiler output
items.note: A steam safety valve is lifted and reseated, not merely inspected — the reseat is half the device.

items.label: STEAM: high steam pressure limit tripped and proven; manual reset verified
STEAM: operating pressure and high-limit setpoint (kPa)
STEAM: safety valve set pressure and reseat pressure (kPa)
items.note: The D row proves the lift; this row records the numbers. The pairing rule — a protective function proves in D and records in E when the same test yields both.

items.label: STEAM: normal water level at operating pressure (mm on the glass)
STEAM: feedwater temperature and conductivity at handover (°C / µS/cm)
items.note: Conductivity at start-up is the baseline every later blowdown decision is argued against.
